YouTube Music has a serious flaw: it keeps feeding you songs you already know over and over again, or ones that sound mostly the same:
"Listen Again", "Forgotten Favorites", "Quick Picks": the experience will be like this for a few hours until you're sick of it: [song you know], [song that sounds... just like the last one?].

Can we fix it? Well probably not as I do not have influence over Google, and I have no idea how a company worth trillions shipped something *this* bad.... buuut we can build our own variety!

First I need a test subject, I chose myself:
We will be downloading a list of tracks to use for this experiment; I chose my music playlist — 676 tracks in my case — for processing. 
This will take hours depending on the size...
[...]
Now that we have them: 
We will split the tracks into 5 second slices and run them all through a specialized music embedding model, a aMuQ-MuLan (mediocre for the sake of demonstration), that, in simple terms, projects every track into latent vector space. 
With this data we can actually see which songs and genres cluster together.

Great! We have all this data, so what can we do with it? :
   Firstly, we can now have queues that are actually diverse! Either fresh relative to what's been playing, or a gradual change across different genres if you'd prefer. Both are possible.
   Secondly, ask for anything: "Romantic", "Chill techno". Because it works with natural language, you can even hook it up to your AI agent and have it manage things for you. 
   Let's say you've had a rough week and don't want any slow songs that will ruin your mood for the next few days, you've had enough classical music for today but your playlist is full of it, or you have 3 albums but don't want to be stuck with them.
  Thirdly, actual discovery: not more of what you already have, but tracks you don't have yet that land close to your taste. Think of it like auto-expanding your queue or discovering on Spotify.
   Fourthly, you can use the data however you want:
   Compare it with friends, collect data on thousands of people and use machine learning to develop a whole new recommendation algorithm, so you never have to see [song you know], [song that sounds the same] again.

records.text:
New blog: Is human taste overrated in harness engineering?

An agent harness is the system around a model. It decides which tools the model can call, what evidence it sees, and what it remembers between steps. Most harnesses are still designed by human taste. Run the agent, read where it failed, change the harness, try again.

That loop is increasingly being automated, with a strong model rewriting the harness itself. So we asked how far that can go. We ran Qwen on three drug design tasks from SMDD-Bench and compared a manually redesigned harness against one produced by automated harness search with Claude in the loop.

No single approach won everywhere. The manual harness pulled clearly ahead when the fix was changing what the agent sees and remembers. Automated search did better once that was in place and the remaining problem was how to search the chemistry itself.

The hard part was rarely implementing the fix. It was diagnosing what kind of failure we were looking at, and that is where human taste still mattered.

Work with @KevinH1119568 , @aviral_kumar2  and @niloofar_mire 

Read more 👇

I wanted ChatGPT's voice mode to know me.

Problem: my whole Obsidian system is built around Claude. The vault, months of memory files, hooks that load my context every session. Claude Code knows my deadlines, my courses, my rules. ChatGPT knew none of it.

Step 1: Codex lives inside the ChatGPT app, has voice, and works right in my vault. I gave it an AGENTS.md: read everything Claude reads. Now it knows me too.

Step 2: they still didn't know what I'd said to each other.

My friend @Kuberwastaken built reference: one MCP server that lets Claude and Codex search each other's past sessions. Great idea. For my setup it had two gaps:

It's pull-only. An agent only remembers if it decides to search.
It skips Codex voice transcripts. Voice was the whole point.

So I fixed both in a small tool that runs next to it: agent-sync.

One hook on each side. Before every message, it hands over whatever I just said to the other agent, voice included. 0.05s, one local Python script, no server.

The test: told Codex by voice "let our codeword be PVC". Switched to Claude, typed "what's my code word, don't read any files".

PVC.

Use them together, they're two halves of one idea:

正式對平台營運方提告。

帳號還透過流量獲得收益。

人的聲音和肖像一樣，都可能是個人身分的象徵

法院因此沒有進一步判定
這188支影片本身是否真的構成侵權。

真正留下影響的，
是日本法院正式把「聲音」放進了
可能受到公眾形象權保護的範圍。
對聲優、歌手、演員來說，AI時代最重要的資產，
可能不只是一張臉，
包括那個一開口就能讓人認出你的聲音。

HBM4若每Gb站上4.5美元，三星的AI記憶體定價權可能明顯升溫。
三星正與主要客戶協商2027年HBM4供應合約，目標單價為每Gb 4至5美元，且至少4.5美元；相較目前約每Gb 1.5美元的HBM3E，合約價可能達約3倍。談判預計在本月進入最後階段，三星也已敲定2027年大部分HBM訂單。

HBM的供應量與價格通常透過年度談判確定。TrendForce指出，AI伺服器需求仍在擴張，但HBM與Conventional DRAM持續爭奪有限的先進製程與晶圓產能；新世代產品的良率、產出提升也需要時間，因此2027年記憶體供應預計仍偏緊。

TrendForce已上修2027年HBM價格展望，預估Blended ASP年增121%。其判斷除了反映供應吃緊，也納入高價HBM4占比提高，以及HBM4E預定於2027年下半年逐步放量的影響。

這不代表所有記憶體產品都會以相同幅度調價，但若長約價格按此方向落定，AI伺服器業者的高頻寬記憶體成本壓力將更集中；對供應商而言，能否提升良率與產出，將是把需求轉成營收的關鍵。

records.text:
安いモデルだけで開発を続けるつもりでも、試作や実験、推論サービスの混雑で想定が変わる。Wagtailの開発者がGLM 5.3 Flashを中心に使おうとした1か月の記録は、モデル選びと仕事の進め方を一緒に考える材料になる。

・前半は対象モデルだけで作業できた。そのモデルの利用費として68ドルを報告し、予算内に収まった。
・後半は別のモデルも使い、月間20億トークンのうち、対象モデルの利用は半分にとどまった。
・MCPサーバーの試作では、モデル選択とエージェントの動かし方が響き、ほぼ一晩で4.5億トークン、150ドルを使ったという。
・推論サービスの性能が低下した際には、DeepSeekやQwenの近いモデルへ切り替えた。切り替えは簡単でも、供給の問題は予想外だった。
・日常業務を一つのモデルへ寄せても、比較評価や新しい手法の実験には複数モデルが必要になる。実験用の予算も別に見積もる。
・次は利用量と費用を継続して測り、目標をどこまでに限定するかや、計画・実装・レビューを担うエージェントの分け方を見直す。

安い単価を選ぶだけでなく、何のための試行にいくら使ったかまで追う。利用したトークン数だけでは、仕事の成果を測れない。

records.text:
発走前 - 10月3日、京都、11レース

十八頭が顔を揃えたこの一戦、記録を並べるとまず一つの事実にぶつかる。SSRはどこも近い——能力の接近した一戦だ。上限の SSR 108 から下限の SSR 100 までわずか八つの幅に収まり、UPI は上限 +1、下限 -0 と横並び。平凡そのものも読みのうちだが、ここまで均整が取れると、かえって個性の輪郭が際立ってくる。

馬群トップのラダー評価 SSR 108 を刻むのはヨシノイースターとヤマニンアルリフラの二頭。通算三十七戦を誇るヨシノイースターは RE -0.80 という分散モデル評価で、三十六戦分の蓄積がそのまま数字に出た格好だ。一方、ヤマニンアルリフラは UPI が直近五戦で 0.87 → 0.70 と冷却中。同じ頂点でも温度差がある。ヒシアイラは UPI +1.0 でこの馬群で最高のユニバーサル記録を持つものの、こちらも直近四戦で 1.39 → 1.01 と下り坂。九十一日ぶりの実戦という条件がどう作用するか。対照的にディアナザールは UPI が 0.57 → 0.64 と上昇曲線を描き、一コーナー平均 1.7 番手から崩れない逃げ粘り型。十八頭中唯一といっていい前傾姿勢が、スロー想定では異彩を放つ。

後方からの仕掛けに目を転じれば、レッドエヴァンスが一コーナー平均 8.2 番手から直線で平均 4.3 ポジションを上げる「後方一気」の典型。タガノアラリアは末脚が平均 34.07 秒と馬群最速の上がりを持ちながら、UPI は 0.41 → 0.24 と冷めている。時計と勢いが噛み合わない歯がゆさを抱えている。

展開の鍵はペースだ。差し馬×スロー想定という枠組みが示す通り、直線が混むほど利が出る構造。先行傾向 0.2984、混沌度 0.693 という数値は、逃げ切りが容易ではないことを物語る。ディアナザールやメイショウヨゾラ（一コーナー平均 2.2 番手）が前を占めたとしても、後ろからレッドエヴァンスやタガノアラリアが雪崩れ込む余地は十分にある。京都芝千二百メートルという舞台は、直線の長さが後方の末脚を拾いやすい。

個々の事情にも触れておこう。リリージョワは UPI が直近四戦で 2.58 → 0.72 と急降下し、百二十六日ぶりの実戦を迎える。デイトナモードも九十八日の空白があり、通算二十二戦の重鎮とはいえ UPI は 0.15 → 0.04 へ。クラスペディアは掲示板率七十パーセント（十戦）の堅実さを持つが、一コーナー平均 2.9 番手の逃げ粘り型がスローでどう機能するか。フロムダスクは SSR 100 と馬群の底に位置し、RE +0.13 と分散モデル評価が唯一のプラス。ここだけ見れば浮いているが、それが伏兵の証になるかどうかは走ってみなければわからない。

A Kilogram of Memory Now Costs as Much as 620 Grams of Gold

South Korea's DRAM exports came to nearly $24bn in August, the highest since records began in 2008 and up 412% from a year earlier.

The number is extreme enough that it needs converting to feel real. In the first 20 days of August, Korea's DRAM export price reached $92,183 per kilogram, up 401% in a year. At current gold prices, a kilogram of memory chips is worth roughly the same as 620 grams of 24-karat gold.

Stretching the time axis shows how this cycle differs from the last ones. Korean DRAM exports peaked at about $8bn to $9bn a month in 2017 and 2018, and around $7bn in 2021. This time they went straight to $24bn, close to three times the previous record, rather than merely returning to an old high.

The 412% itself is flattered by the starting point. 2025 was the trough for memory, with monthly exports dipping into the $4bn range, and anything measured from there looks good.

Price is not the whole story either. Export value grew faster than export prices, which means volumes rose too. Once AI servers absorbed the capacity for high-bandwidth memory, chips for ordinary servers and PCs got tight as well, and spot prices now sit 44% above contract prices. Price and volume moving together is why the revenue figure jumped this far.

Source: Korea trade statistics, Goldman Sachs and TrendForce (Image: @glocalinvestor)

I think the Neocloud thesis is getting stronger.

The most important signal to me is that GPU pricing power is no longer just a $NBIS story.

Nebius raised H100/H200/B200/B300 pricing by roughly 17–21%, and now AWS is also raising high-end GPU pricing.

That suggests the underlying driver is broader:

Compute remains scarce.

For $NBIS, this is the cleaner setup.

Higher GPU pricing → Higher revenue/GPU → Better utilization economics → Faster payback

And it gets that upside with a much cleaner financing profile.

$CRWV is different.

Its biggest weakness has always been Capital, not demand.

But now we are starting to see the financial infrastructure around AI evolve — converts, GPU-backed financing, sale-leasebacks and potentially residual-value protection.

Even AWS is exploring GPU sale-leaseback structures.

To me, that matters a lot for $CRWV.

Compute was the bottleneck.
Capital became the bottleneck.
Now the market is starting to build solutions for the Capital bottleneck.

So I still see:

$NBIS = cleaner risk-adjusted setup.
$CRWV = higher-convexity setup if funding costs fall.

And as long as GPU pricing remains strong while financing infrastructure keeps improving, I remain bullish on both.

J.P. Morgan: 
Cooling Content for NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra and AWS Trainium 3 Liquid-Cooled Racks Increases Significantly

​I. NVIDIA NVL72 Rack Cooling Content
​Excluding the CDU, the cooling content per rack is approximately:
​GB300 NVL72: ~$48,250
​Vera Rubin NVL72: ~$66,250
​Vera Rubin Ultra (VRU) NVL72: ~$98,500
​GPU TDP is rising from 1,400W (GB300) to 2,300W (Vera Rubin), potentially reaching ~2,600W (VRU). Regarding mass production schedules, VRU may arrive in the second half of 2027, serving as a key milestone for observing the deployment of rack-level thermal management.
​Compute Trays (18 per rack)
​GB300: ~$1,500 per tray
​Vera Rubin: $2,000–$2,500
​VRU: $3,000–$3,500
​VRU is switching to double-sided cold plates: The Bianca module requires 6 cold plates (2 on the front, 4 on the back), plus cold plates for the CX-9 and PDB. Vertical power delivery pushes power components and SOCAMM to the back of the board, necessitating double-sided cooling. Additionally, diamond-copper materials are placed above the HBM to improve thermal conductivity, pushing up the unit price.
​Switch Trays
​GB300 / Vera Rubin: 9 each
​VRU: Still 9, but upgraded to 1.5U, dual-layer boards, with cooling content exceeding $3,000 per tray.
​Rack Manifold: Remains around $10,000 across all three generations.
​II. Quick Disconnect (QD) Value Roughly Doubles
​QD content per rack is approximately:
​GB300: ~$9,400
​Vera Rubin: ~$11,000
​VRU: ~$20,500 (~100% increase compared to Vera Rubin)
​The primary driver is the upgrade from older UQD/MQD to zero-drip ZQD, which carries roughly double the unit price.
​VRU Configuration Highlights:
​Compute Trays: Internal 12 MQD + 8 ZQD06 + 8 miniQD; External 2 ZQD14. The QD value is ~$750 per tray.
​Switch Trays: Dual-layer boards with a total of 8 MQD; External 2 ZQD14.
​44U Rack Manifold: 88 receptacles upgraded from UQD08 to high-flow ZQD14.
​Suppliers like Fositek may benefit from gross margin improvements. The primary focus remains the mass production progress in 2H 2027.
​III. Rubin Ultra GPU Heat Spreader Content Increases 4–5x
​Assuming standard Rubin unit price as x:
​B300: 0.6x, one-piece integrated cover.
​Rubin: 1.0x, one-piece integrated but larger in size.
​Rubin Ultra: 4.0x–5.0x, redesigned as a detachable three-piece set (stiffener + temporary lid + multiple screws).
​The detachable lid is utilized first during advanced packaging and testing phases. At the ODM stage, the lid is removed, allowing the liquid cold plate to press directly onto the TIM1.5 interface. Jentech is noted as the primary supplier. Small-volume trial production for Rubin is expected around Q4 2026, while Rubin Ultra heat spreader mass production may occur in Q1–Q2 2027. If adoption remains stuck at trial production without rapid, full-scale deployment, the ~50x forward P/E ratio could present valuation risks. Tracking 2026 trial yields and packaging pass rates is critical.
​IV. AWS Trainium 3 Liquid-Cooled Racks Are Actually More Expensive Than Vera Rubin
​The AWS Trainium 3 (Teton3 MAX/NRL72) single-rack cooling content is ~$86,000, which is higher than NVIDIA Vera Rubin's ~$66,250. Although the Trainium 3 ASIC TDP is only 700W (compared to the GPU's 2,300W), the thermal design is much more aggressive.
​Comparison Highlights:
​Compute Trays (both have 18): Trainium 3 is $3,000–$3,500 per tray (4 ASICs use 8 double-sided cold plates, plus 1 tray-level base cold plate and 22 QDs); Vera Rubin is $2,000–$2,500.
​Switch Trays: Trainium 3 has 10, whereas Vera Rubin has 9; the unit price is the same at $1,500–$2,000.
​QDs: A single Trainium 3 rack features ~512 QDs, valued at ~$10,200.
​The report lists mass production schedules for both around Q3/Q4 2026. Liquid cooling suppliers such as AVC and Fositek are poised to see a volume ramp-up, with multi-rack cluster expansion serving as the actual catalyst for shipments.
